Write data and the scales that index it to one folder

Source: R/dataset.R
write_scale_dataset.Rd

The data is written as a hive-partitioned Arrow IPC dataset and the scales travel with it, so open_scale_dataset() gives back both and the result can be recast without re-declaring anything. Each scale is stored as the definition write_scale() writes, so its attributes and aliases travel too.

write_scale_dataset(
  data,
  x,
  path,
  partitioning = NULL,
  compression = "zstd",
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

The table to write, in any supported backend.

x

The NestedScale or ScaleProduct the data is indexed by.

path

Directory to create. It must not already contain a store unless overwrite = TRUE.

partitioning

Columns to partition the data by (hive style). NULL (default) picks nothing; a good choice is a low-cardinality identifier such as a year, which lets a filtered read skip whole files.

compression

Codec for the IPC files, e.g. "zstd" (default), "lz4" or "uncompressed". If the codec is unavailable in the installed Arrow build, the files are written uncompressed with a warning.

overwrite

Replace an existing store at path.

Value

path, invisibly.

Examples

p <- scale_product(a = scale_example(), b = scale_example2())
d <- merge(
  data.frame(unit = c("U1", "U2")),
  data.frame(period = c("p1", "p2"))
)
d$v <- 1:4
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "store")
if (requireNamespace("arrow", quietly = TRUE)) {
  write_scale_dataset(d, p, dir, overwrite = TRUE)
  ds <- open_scale_dataset(dir)
  ds
}
#> <scale_dataset> C:\Users\admin\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpM9FXpU/store 
#>   rows:  4
#>   files: 1 (1 KB)
#>   scale: product over a x b
